title: Tokens in 60 seconds
caption: Tokens in 60 seconds: what a language model actually reads, and why it is priced and limited in tokens, not words.

scenes.say: A language model doesn't read letters, and it doesn't read words. It reads tokens.
A token is a chunk of text. Common words are one token. Rare words get split into pieces.
And tokens are the unit for everything.

items.title: Price
items.say: APIs charge per token, in and out.

items.title: Limits
items.say: Context windows are measured in tokens.

items.title: Spelling
items.say: And it's why models stumble at counting the letters in a word.

scenes.text:
Models don't read words.
*They read tokens.*
scenes.say: In English, a token is roughly three quarters of a word. That's tokens.
